text: North America: US stocks slipped Friday, led by a second straight drop in tech. The S&P 500 fell 0.4% to 7,562, the Nasdaq fell 0.9% and the Dow edged up 0.1%. Nvidia fell again after its CEO resigned, and Treasury yields rose. Most sectors outside tech finished higher, and the S&P 500 still gained 2.5% on the week, its first winning week since early October. Canada was steadier: the TSX closed at 36,106, down 0.1%. Elsewhere: European markets were mixed, and I could not verify Asia's close.
mood: Cautious, not panicked. The worry is concentrated in AI and tech, which is a big part of the US market but a smaller part of the TSX and Europe. The rest held up and the week was still positive.
veqt: VEQT is mostly US and Canadian stocks plus international, so North America drives it. A tech-led dip moves it far less than the Nasdaq, and the TSX barely moved.
label: Slightly bearish today
